AdcQuad.summary: The selected DCV quadratic coefficient contributes a square term when the quadratic mode byte is enabled.
limitations: Other modes use the affine path; overload guards can bypass the final consumer.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded DCV quadratic branch

lifecycle.scope: 34411A APP 2.43, bounded DCV 10 V calibration and reading paths.

calculation.text: GandalfDcvFunction::calGain calculates q in the 10 V negative-reference branch. Let v be the current negative reference value in volts, p the saved positive-point sample, and m the current negative-point sample. Both samples are divided by total packet weight and corrected by the selected terminal offset. Firmware calculates a=(p+m)/(2*v*v), b=(p-m)/(-2*v), then q=-a/b. It requires a nonzero saved p and checks -1e-6 <= 1/b <= 1e-6 before writing AdcQuad; upstream checks also apply. This formula uses the current v for both polarities; it does not independently fit unequal positive/negative reference magnitudes. The preceding positive-point branch saves p and calculates gain as (v/p)/(1+q_old*v).

application.text: After the DCV linear gain/offset stage, PPC computes V=V0+q*(V0*V0) when the quadratic stage is enabled. q has units 1/V. The correction is deltaV=q*V0*V0; the equivalent reading-dependent multiplier is 1+q*V0. For example, q=5e-8 1/V adds 5 microvolts at either V0=+10 V or V0=-10 V. The coefficient is used by the PPC reading calculation, not loaded as an ADC FPGA correction register.

selection.text: The checked DCV getter enables the quadratic stage for range index 2 (10 V). AdcQuad is one shared scalar, while the preceding offset is selected for Front or Rear terminals. This is a quadratic reading correction, not a per-code ADC INL table.

activation.text: calGain writes the registered DcvConstants scalar through setOnly. The getter and reading-configuration path forward it to the PPC calculation. CAL export serializes current registered values in memory; CAL:STORE separately writes that group to NOR. A successful scalar write alone does not establish a NOR commit. The complete post-adjustment refresh sequence is not established here.

related.text: DcvGain10 and the selected DcvOff10 define V0. The calibration producer uses the selected offset when preparing p and m, and the positive gain adjustment depends on the previous AdcQuad value. Keep these values together when interpreting a CAL set.

lifecycle.scope: 34411A APP 2.43 and the bounded ADC FPGA paths described in the evidence. Static use does not prove delivery or execution on a connected instrument.

calculation.text: fineDcCancel starts from D = trunc(the current DcOffset). In each sweep it tries D-2, D-1, D, D+1 and D+2, writes each candidate to the working CAL state, synchronizes hardware and acquires an internal calibration result m. For ordinary finite results it requires m to increase strictly with D, then selects the first candidate minimizing abs(m). If the center wins, the search succeeds and writes the selected D again; otherwise it repeats around the new center. Acquisition failure, a failed monotonicity check or exhaustion of 10 sweeps causes failure. This is an internal zero-centering search, not a direct voltage-offset conversion. The selected setup refers to the registered ADC CAL object. Updating D changes its working value; saving it to NOR is a separate operation. Automatic execution at startup and the complete outer failure/rollback policy are not established by this card.

application.text: D = trunc(DcOffset), P = trunc(PiOffset), where trunc removes the fractional part toward zero. The 64-entry table is offset[2k] = D+P and offset[2k+1] = D-P for k=0..31. APP sends the low 16 bits of each entry to the offset-table writer, starting at selector 0x0200. The FPGA uses signed low-7-bit values, read with its feedback address sequence. They combine with the coarse feedback-table contribution and digital modulation before the feedback code is limited and retained for merge.

selection.text: Separate DCV, ACV and ACI CAL states exist. The suffix identifies the ADC setup, not the active instrument configuration. Use the coefficients from the same setup together; a single CAL file does not identify which setup is currently active.

activation.text: AdcCalConfig::setConfig calls calculateRegValues to build working values; configAdc sends the calculated fields and tables. Writing a scalar, sending FPGA configuration and committing CAL to NOR are separate steps. CAL export serializes the current registered CAL state in memory. CAL:STORE uses the same CAL group to write a NOR record; an exported file alone does not prove that its values have already been committed to NOR. The complete activation sequence after external CAL import has not yet been verified.

related.text: PiOffset sets the alternating part of the same 64-entry table. LutGain and Jitter contribute to the feedback calculation; FineMergeGain uses the resulting retained feedback history.

application.text: For the supported finite nonnegative range 0 <= g < 1/64, G = low10(round_half_away(g*65536)); k = G/65536. APP calculates a register value and configAdc passes it to the FPGA. In the ordinary merge path, without overflow or truncation loss, delta_fine = previous_fine - current_fine and M = 65536*C_history + G*delta_fine. C_history is the retained feedback code from the matching pipeline history, not the current raw coarse sample. The exact RTL uses finite-width slices; this algebraic form does not replace those rules. G changes the fine contribution, not the complete reading scale.

Adc_PiOffset.summary: PiOffset P sets the alternating component of the ADC offset LUT: D+P and D−P.
limitations: It is not a direct reading offset or an established cancellation of the analog geometry term.

Divider10M.summary: A conditional correction for ordinary high-range resistance results, applied below its checked guard.
limitations: Above the guard the path selects overload; a global override changes the additional upper limit.

evidence.scope: APP11 bounded ordinary RES range 6/7 path

lifecycle.scope: 34411A APP 2.43; bounded resistance calibration and high-range correction paths.

calculation.text: In the range-index-5 (10 Mohm) branch, calGain first updates the gain banks, then installs a dedicated divider calibration front-end configuration and acquires another sample. If acquisition succeeds and the sample lies between 8 Mohm and 12 Mohm inclusive, the sample is written directly as Divider10M. There is no further arithmetic between this sample and the scalar setter. These are firmware acceptance bounds, not accuracy limits. The complete upstream sample-processing and physical switch network are outside this bounded trace.

application.text: Let D be Divider10M and x the nonnegative result after the resistance linear and absolute-value stages. The enabled high-range stage calculates R=x*D/(D-x). D and x are in ohms. The checked consumer requires x < 0.9999*D; overload and other reading guards still apply. D is an effective divider resistance, not a constant multiplier on the displayed resistance. During high-range gain calibration the inverse expression x=R*D/(D+R) also appears.

selection.text: The ordinary 100 Mohm and 1 Gohm paths enable the divider correction (range indices 6 and 7). One Divider10M scalar is shared; there are no separate Front/Rear or 2-wire/4-wire copies of this field. This does not establish which range/mode combinations are available on a connected instrument.

activation.text: The accepted sample replaces the registered Divider10M value through setOnly. The resistance coefficient path reads that value for the PPC calculation. CAL export serializes the current CAL group in memory; CAL:STORE separately saves it to NOR. The scalar write alone does not prove a NOR commit or immediate refresh of every working consumer.

related.text: The selected ResGain/Res4Gain and Front/Rear offset determine x before divider correction. calculation.text: calGain computes G_new=G_old*reference/sample, using the current FreqGain and a captured debug-reading scalar. These are firmware acceptance bounds, not measurement accuracy limits or a recommended calibration procedure. The passing branch writes the registered FreqGain scalar through setOnly. The full upstream sample-processing and command-dispatch chain is not established by this card.

application.text: Firmware sets Fbase=106250000*G Hz. In the ordinary counter branch, dt=(B-A)/Fbase, frequency=N/dt and period=dt/N, where A, B and N are the supplied counter values. selection.text: One FreqGain scalar is shared by the frequency and period calculations; it is not a separate coefficient for every range or terminal.

activation.text: The scalar setter changes registered CAL memory. setFrequencyGain transfers the scaled value to FrequencyCompute. Export reads current CAL memory; CAL:STORE separately saves the group to NOR. The complete refresh sequence after external CAL import remains unresolved.

related.text: The capacitance calculation also consumes FreqGain in its denominator path. Interpret it as part of the same CAL set, rather than as an isolated change affecting frequency only.

The linear stage is y0 = double_signed(wrap64(S - o)) * g. trunc means conversion toward zero within the supported numeric domain. These coefficients are applied by PPC software in this path; the endpoint is a reading calculation, not a directly programmed FPGA gain/offset register. Resistance uses an absolute-value stage. On ordinary 100 Mohm and 1 Gohm ranges, the enabled divider stage uses y*D/(D-y), where D is Divider10M; its guards and overload branches still apply.

selection.text: 2-wire resistance selects the range-specific gain and the Front or Rear offset. Gain is shared between Front and Rear. Separate 2-wire/4-wire banks are used. Offset compensation selects an OC bank for range indices 0..2; the other ranges use the ordinary bank.

activation.text: The function's syncSoftware path obtains the selected coefficients and passes them to setCalCoeffs. The exact event and timing that activate values after a CAL import are not yet verified. CAL export serializes the current registered values in memory; CAL:STORE separately saves that group to NOR. A successful scalar update does not itself establish a NOR commit.

related.text: The matching ResOff (Front or Rear) for the same range and OC setting participates in the same linear-stage formula. Divider10M additionally affects the ordinary 100 Mohm and 1 Gohm paths.

limitations: These are vectors, not individually known frequency taps; firmware writes do not prove FPGA acceptance or an instrument frequency response.

calculation.text: The checked APP11 evidence binds 770 stored ACV/ACI flatness rows to named holders and the ordinary writer, but does not close how every vector is measured or fitted. application.text: The ordinary firmware writer passes vector entries as signed low-16-bit words to the control path. A stored vector is consumed as a sequence; an individual entry is not assigned an independently proven frequency tap, and firmware requests do not prove FPGA acceptance.

selection.text: APP11 binds distinct ACI and ACV vectors by range/profile holders. Exact active vector, tap count, clock/profile conditions, and complete hardware response depend on configuration and remain bounded by the respective evidence.

activation.text: The ordinary writer issues the software coefficient requests from the current holders. The source evidence does not prove FPGA acceptance, complete atomic activation, or an instrument frequency response after CAL import.

selection.text: APP11 has two separate 70-entry holders: AciLpFilter, shared across ACI ranges, and AcvLpFilter, shared across ACV ranges. The corresponding function sync selects its holder; these vectors are not one vector shared between ACI and ACV.
